The original Apple TV 4K launched in 2017 has just been added to Apple's list of "vintage" products. Find out what that means right now.

The original Apple TV 4K has been listed as a "vintage" product, and repair services may be reduced.

If you're still using the first-generation Apple TV 4K, released nearly a decade ago, getting it repaired may become a lot more difficult.

According to MacRumors, Apple has marked the original Apple TV 4K as a "vintage" product.

Apple maintains a list of vintage and obsolete products on its website.

  • "Vintage" means more than five years have passed since the product was discontinued.
  • "Obsolete" means more than seven years have passed since it was discontinued.

If your product is marked as "obsolete," Apple will no longer offer any repair service.

If marked as "vintage," Apple can still provide repairs in most cases, depending on parts availability.

So if you still have the original Apple TV 4K and might need repairs, you should act fast. Of course, you can also keep an eye out for the new Apple TV 4K expected to be announced at next Tuesday's "Welcome home" event.

Are you still using the first-generation Apple TV 4K? Let us know in the comments.
